title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing an 'atelier spatial', a workshop of geometric figures. The figures form a set A. They carry two relations: X ⊴ Y ('X is a sub-figure of Y') and X |o| Y (on this and the neighbouring pages, 'interior disjointness'). The previous page checked axioms Ax 1-4 of an earlier, longer formulation, using a relation ∘≪ and the 'Dép' (dépliage?) construction. This page summarizes the result: an atelier spatial is equivalent to a triple (A, ⊴, |o|) with three axioms.

Axiom 1: (a) ⊴ is a partial order; (b) |o| is symmetric and (most likely, see corrections) anti-reflexive.

Axiom 2: compatibility between ⊴ and |o|. As transcribed it reads 'X ⊴ Y ⇒ X |o| Y'. For a disjointness relation the sensible statement is 'X ⊴ Y ⇒ not X |o| Y': a figure is never interior-disjoint from a figure it lies in.

Axiom 3 (separation / extensionality): define, for Y ∈ A, Y° = {Z ∈ A : ∀Z′, Z′ |o| Y ⇒ Z′ |o| Z}. So Z ∈ Y° iff Z^⊥ ⊇ Y^⊥, i.e. Z lies in the biorthogonal closure of Y for the orthogonality |o|. Each X then gives the 'figure' Dép X = {X′° : X′ ⊴ X} ⊂ P(A). Dép X is ordered by the order induced from X̄ = {X′ : X′ ⊴ X}. The map X ↦ Dép X into ordered subsets ('figures') of P(A) must be injective. So a figure is determined by the system of closed 'regions' of its sub-figures.

Grothendieck then announces a reformulation with Σ = Σ_A as base set. The Σ_A are presumably the |o|-closed parts, compare the previous page: 'the largest element of Dép X … S |o| T in Σ'. He defines a 'spatiale (ensembliste)' as a triple (Σ, ≤, C): Σ a set, ≤ an order on Σ, C a map Σ → Σ. The next page gives the axioms: complete lattice; C an involutive order-antiautomorphism; x ∧ Cx = 0. That is exactly a complete ortholattice, with X |o| Y :⇔ X ≤ CY as the orthogonality relation.

Purpose: to replace the 'figure-level' data (A, ⊴, |o|) by a lattice of regions with orthocomplement. This is a pointless / mereotopological foundation for the 'ateliers' of tame or elementary geometry Grothendieck was developing in 1986.
errors: Axiom 1b as machine-transcribed ('symétrique et réflexive') is inconsistent with the rest of the development. On the next page |o| is anti-reflexive on Σ* (X |o| X ⇔ X = 0), and on the previous page it is downward-closed, i.e. a disjointness relation. The image most likely reads 'antiréflexive'.
Axiom 2 as transcribed ('X ⊴ Y ⇒ X |o| Y') would make every figure disjoint from its sub-figures, absurd for a disjointness relation. Probably 'on a non X |o| Y', or a slip by Grothendieck.

The target of the map in Axiom 3 ('Fig ens(P(A))', with a struck-out symbol) is not defined on this page. Injectivity is stated, but nothing is said about how the order on Dép X relates to inclusion of the X′°. This is a gap filled only implicitly by the reformulation via Σ.

Spat 1-3 (next page) do not impose orthomodularity or distributivity. Without that, the passage back from Σ to an atelier, i.e. recovering ⊴ on figures, is not guaranteed. The equivalence of the two descriptions is announced, not proved here.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing a geometric 'workshop' of figures by a sub-figure order and an interior-disjointness relation
ideas.modern_name: mereotopology / region-based theory of space (part-of + disjointness or connection relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead (1929), Tarski (1929 geometry of solids), de Laguna; later Clarke (1981), the Region Connection Calculus (Randell–Cui–Cohn 1992)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for a tame topology but contains no such axioms

ideas.what: Y° = {Z : every Z′ disjoint from Y is disjoint from Z}, a biorthogonal closure
ideas.modern_name: biorthogonal (Galois / polarity) closure Y^⊥⊥ of an orthogonality space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, Lattice Theory 1940); Dacey (1968), Foulis–Randall orthogonality spaces

ideas.what: Separation axiom: a figure is determined by the closed regions of its sub-figures (injectivity of X ↦ Dép X)
Reformulation as a 'spatiale': complete lattice with an involutive antiautomorphism C satisfying x ∧ Cx = 0, and orthogonality X ≤ CY
ideas.modern_name: complete ortholattice (orthocomplemented lattice), e.g. regular open algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936), Birkhoff (1940); Tarski regular open algebras

missed.claim: Grothendieck's foundation of 'ateliers spatiaux' (tame geometry of figures) is built on exactly the machinery of orthogonality spaces and complete ortholattices used in quantum logic and in point-free mereotopology. He reaches it via figures and interior disjointness rather than via Hilbert-space orthogonality or regular open sets. The literature on Grothendieck's tame topology program does not connect it to mereotopology or ortholattice theory.
missed.quote: Y° = {Z ∈ A | ∀Z′ ∈ A, Z′|o|Y ⇒ Z′|o|Z} … Appelons spatiale (ensembliste) un triple (Σ, ≤, C)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a documented link between Grothendieck's 1986 'ateliers' and region-based / point-free geometry (contact algebras, RCC). It is of interest to historians of the tame-topology program and to people working on point-free foundations of o-minimal-type geometry.

missed.claim: The claimed equivalence between the figure-level structure (A, ⊴, |o|) with Axioms 1-3 and the lattice-level 'spatiale' (Σ, ≤, C) is only announced. There is no reconstruction theorem recovering A from Σ, and no discussion of which extra conditions (orthomodularity, Boolean/regular-open case) are needed.
missed.quote: Je vais essayer de reformuler la structure, avec Σ = Σ_A comme ensemble de base.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A precise representation theorem for 'ateliers' in terms of ortholattices would be a small but genuine result in mereotopology. It is unclear whether Grothendieck's later pages complete it.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics itself (biorthogonal closure, complete ortholattices) is classical. Grothendieck is rediscovering standard material. What is notable is the unpublished context: a 1986 axiomatization of geometric 'workshops' via part-of and interior disjointness, i.e. Grothendieck doing mereotopology. This is essentially absent from accounts of his work.
transcription_corrections: Axiom 1b: 'symétrique et réflexive' is probably 'symétrique et antiréflexive' (the image shows '...-tiréflexive').
Axiom 2: possibly 'Si X ⊴ Y, on a non X |o| Y'. The small mark before X|o|Y may be a negation, or Grothendieck's own slip.
The target 'Fig ens(P(A))' is uncertain. It may read 'Fig ord(P(A))' or similar, after a struck-out symbol.
The marginal insertion reads approximately: 'et relations d'ordre sur Dép X déduites de celles de X̄ = {X′ ∈ A | X′ ⊴ X}', followed by '(bien sûr, ayant posé, pour Y ∈ A, ...)'.
